instrument.note: code_head is the tree this run STARTED from; it may predate the commit that carries this file, so the sha256 is what a re-run keys on

purpose: does a session-hierarchy structure exist for the #4211 candidate-expansion arm to walk?

definitions.hierarchy_linked_turn: a turn Point reachable from its Session via (:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Point) — the edge the scoping doc's arm walks
definitions.entity_linked_turn: a turn Point carrying (:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) — entity attachment, NOT the hierarchy
definitions.event_level_attachment: an :Event carries a session_id PROPERTY, so (:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) is a session->entity attachment with NO Session->Object edge; counted separately, never folded into the Session counts

edges_the_arm_could_walk.contains: the hierarchy (Session -> turns) the scoping doc's arm uses
edges_the_arm_could_walk.aboutObject: entity attachment; the edge the #4211 gate names. NOT the hierarchy — a graph can have one and not the other

queries.nodes_by_label: MATCH (n) UNWIND labels(n) AS l RETURN l AS label, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
queries.edges_by_type: MATCH ()-[r]->() RETURN type(r) AS edge, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
queries.aboutObject_by_endpoint: MATCH (s)-[r:aboutObject]->(o) UNWIND labels(s) AS sl RETURN sl AS src_label, labels(o) AS dst_labels, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
queries.turns_total: MATCH (p:Point) WHERE coalesce(p.is_episodic,false)=true AND p.pointKind='event' RETURN count(p) AS n
queries.episodic_points_any_kind: MATCH (p:Point) WHERE coalesce(p.is_episodic, false) = true RETURN count(p) AS n
queries.turns_with_aboutObject: MATCH (p:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) WHERE coalesce(p.is_episodic,false)=true AND p.pointKind='event' RETURN count(DISTINCT p) AS n
queries.nonepisodic_points_with_aboutObject: MATCH (p:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) WHERE coalesce(p.is_episodic, false) = false RETURN count(DISTINCT p) AS n
queries.sessions_with_aboutObject: MATCH (s:Session)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) RETURN count(DISTINCT s) AS n
queries.contains_distinct_pairs: MATCH (s:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(p:Point) RETURN count(DISTINCT s.id + '|' + p.id) AS n
queries.contains_duplicate_pairs: MATCH (s:Session)-[r:CONTAINS]->(p:Point) WITH s, p, count(r) AS c WHERE c > 1 RETURN count(*) AS n
queries.sessions_with_contains: MATCH (s:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Point) RETURN count(DISTINCT s) AS n
queries.contains_targets_by_kind: MATCH (:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(p:Point) RETURN p.pointKind AS pointKind, coalesce(p.is_episodic, false) AS episodic, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
queries.sessions_with_gt1_contains_turn: MATCH (s:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(p:Point) WITH s, count(DISTINCT p) AS c WHERE c > 1 RETURN count(*) AS n
queries.sessions_with_gt1_entity_linked_turn: MATCH (s:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(p:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) WITH s, count(DISTINCT p) AS c WHERE c > 1 RETURN count(*) AS n
queries.sessions_with_gt1_aboutObject_edge: MATCH (s:Session)-[:aboutObject]->(o:Object) WITH s, count(DISTINCT o) AS c WHERE c > 1 RETURN count(*) AS n
queries.turns_per_session_contains_max_avg: MATCH (s:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(p:Point) WITH s, count(DISTINCT p) AS c RETURN max(c) AS max_c, toFloat(sum(c)) / count(s) AS avg_c
queries.session_signature: MATCH (s:Session) WITH keys(s) AS k, count(*) AS n RETURN k, n ORDER BY n DESC
queries.objects_with_gt1_turn: MATCH (t:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(o:Object) WITH o, count(DISTINCT t) AS c WHERE c > 1 RETURN count(*) AS n
queries.objects_reaching_gt1_session: MATCH (s:Session)-[:aboutObject]->(o:Object) WITH o, count(DISTINCT s) AS c WHERE c > 1 RETURN count(*) AS n
queries.objects_with_point_attachment: MATCH (o:Object) WHERE (:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(o) RETURN count(o) AS n
queries.objects_with_any_attachment: MATCH (o:Object) WHERE ()-[:aboutObject]->(o) RETURN count(o) AS n
queries.events_with_aboutObject: MATCH (e:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) RETURN count(DISTINCT e) AS n
queries.event_session_ids_distinct: MATCH (e:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) RETURN count(DISTINCT e.session_id) AS n
queries.events_without_session_id: MATCH (e:Event) WHERE e.session_id IS NULL RETURN count(e) AS n
queries.events_with_aboutObject_missing_session_: MATCH (e:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) WHERE e.session_id IS NULL RETURN count(e) AS n
queries.objects_reaching_gt1_event: MATCH (:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(o:Object) WITH o, count(*) AS c WHERE c > 1 RETURN count(*) AS n
queries.event_objects_total_distinct: MATCH (:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(o:Object) RETURN count(DISTINCT o) AS n

corpus.ref_density_note: a turn 'names a ref' when the PRODUCTION resolver session_link.extract_refs matches; it can still resolve to nothing if no matching Object exists in the graph

post_measurement_revision.why: The #13919 review found three defects that are fixed in the tool AFTER this run: (1) the three keys named *turn* did not apply the turn discriminator; (2) the `instrument` arm silently dropped a graph on ANY query error, so a shrunken denominator was indistinguishable from a clean census; (3) an unmeasurable run exited 0 behind a NESTED flag. The numbers above were produced by the revision at instrument.sha256 088b7de91e0a (code_head 447180bbc0), which is no longer the file at HEAD. They are NOT retro-edited: a measured artifact records what the instrument that produced it computed.

values_a_rerun_on_this_population_would_.writer.turns_per_session_contains_max_av: published [[9, 8.33333333333333]] (every CONTAINS-wired Point counted); with the turn filter it is [[8, 7.333333333333333]], derived from arms.writer.per_session (contains_turns 8/8/6 vs contains_points_all_kinds 9/9/7 — the 3 statement Points listed in arms.writer.counts.contains_targets_by_kind)
values_a_rerun_on_this_population_would_.sessions_with_gt1_contains_turn: UNCHANGED on this population: store 1 and writer 3 are the same filtered or unfiltered, because every session here CONTAINS at least six turn Points (arms.writer.per_session contains_turns 8/8/6; the store's 27 CONTAINS targets are all pointKind='event')
values_a_rerun_on_this_population_would_.sessions_with_gt1_entity_linked_turn: UNCHANGED on this population for the same reason (writer 2, store 0)

post_measurement_revision.denominator_not_retroactively_verifiable: the instrument arm reported graphs_with_turn_store 60 of 173 and carried NO skipped/error field, so whether any of the 113 unmeasured graphs RAISED a query is UNKNOWN for this run. '0 aboutObject in 60 of 60' is a true statement about the 60 measured graphs; from this artifact alone it is not a statement that the denominator was complete. The tool now publishes graphs_without_turn_store, graphs_skipped_on_error and skipped_on_error, and marks the arm unmeasurable when that last list is non-empty.
post_measurement_revision.action: re-running the instrument regenerates this receipt. No re-run was performed by the review fix: the population it measured (a 1538-session embedded store and a 60-graph instance on another host) is not present on the fixing host, and substituting a different population would be a different measurement.

second_review_round.why: A SECOND review round at the same head (#13919) found seven further defects, all fixed in the tool AFTER this run. None is retro-applied: a measured artifact records what the instrument that produced it computed.

not_in_this_receipt.object_kinds: the Object kind mix (the body's 'dev:issue x 469 / pm:audit_entry / artifact / 0 pm:issue') had NO query in QUERIES, so the inference 'no indexer wrote these => legacy population' is NOT reproducible from this artifact. `object_kinds` now exists; a re-run carries it. The body claim is marked as an unsupported inference for THIS receipt.
not_in_this_receipt.session_created_at_range: same for 'created_at spanning 2026-08-10 -> 2026-09-18': min/max were never asked. `session_created_at_range` now exists.
not_in_this_receipt.per_graph_omitted: per_graph was cut to 25 of the 60 measured rows with no marker (len(per_graph)=25, graphs_with_turn_store=60). The current tool publishes `per_graph_omitted`; this run did not.
not_in_this_receipt.every_graph_has_fewer_turns_than_contain: true here over a non-empty population, so the value stands; the defect was `all([])` returning true over ZERO graphs, which this run did not exercise.
not_in_this_receipt.pair_count_guard: the round-2 multiplicity guard -- `contains_distinct_pairs` / `contains_duplicate_pairs`, re-measured above as 37,605 = 37,605 with 0 duplicates -- was itself NULL-BLIND: the query counted `DISTINCT s.id + '|' + p.id`, and a Point with no `id` property concatenates to null, so `count(DISTINCT null)` is 0. On any graph whose Points carry no id (the fixture-seeder shape this arm measures) the column reads 0 pairs beside a non-zero edge count and the duplicate check reports 0 unconditionally. MEASURED on an embedded fixture (one Session, one pointKind='event' Point with no id, one duplicate CONTAINS): 2 edges -> id-concat 0, `WITH DISTINCT s, p` 1. Fixed to node identity in both copies (the query set and the census arm). This run's own 37,605/37,605 is UNAFFECTED (those Points carry ids), and remains as measured.

second_review_round.provenance_defects_fixed: source_sha256 hashed the COPY after the embedded engine opened it while source_bytes read the ORIGINAL (now one pass over the original, plus `copy_matches_source`); the store arm imported the redislite client directly (redis-guard pattern 2) and never closed the server before rmtree (now through `tortoise.FalkorDB`, closed first); the writer arm mutated whatever TORTOISE_DB_URI named while sitting in the DEFAULT arm set (now opt-in, refusing a non-ephemeral graph name, recording host/port/graph but never the password); the receipt pinned only the tool's bytes (now `instrument.measured_through` = sha256 of tortoise/sdk.py and tortoise/session_link.py).
